GERMAN — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: GERMAN
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.

2. When practising Reading aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading aloud.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading aloud.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading aloud.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading aloud.

3. German for “school” is: (1 mark)
   A. Schule
   B. Wasser
   C. Buch
   D. Haus

4. When practising Selective Listening, Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.

5. When practising Phonological awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological awareness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonological awareness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological awareness.

6. When practising Guided Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Guided Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Guided Reading.

7. When practising Listening for gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for gist.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for gist.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for gist.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.

8. When practising Oral expressions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral expressions.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expressions.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expressions.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Oral expressions.

9. When practising Guided reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Guided reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Guided reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Guided reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided reading.

10. “Guten Tag” means: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Please
   C. Good day / hello
   D. Good night

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Creative writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Functional writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Creative writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Functional writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Guided writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Selective Listening, Imitative speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
